subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.6 cron migration: jobs migrated from jobs.json have blank agent_id — scheduler silently skips them

question: For legacy cron jobs imported without `agentId`, should migration persist the configured default agent as the canonical owner, or should those rows remain ownerless and rely on runtime default-agent fallback?
rationale: Both choices are compatibility-sensitive for multi-agent installs: stamping a concrete owner fixes blank persisted rows but can freeze ownership to the migration-time default, while preserving ownerless rows keeps dynamic fallback semantics but leaves the reported SQLite shape unresolved.

options.title: Persist Config-Aware Default Owner
options.body: Repair doctor/gateway legacy migration to stamp the configured default agent for missing `agentId`, with regression tests and live upgrade proof for migrated rows and scheduled dispatch.

options.title: Keep Ownerless Fallback
options.body: Keep `agent_id` nullable, document ownerless legacy rows as default-agent fallback state, and close or redirect the issue once maintainers accept that behavior.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Migration Tracker
options.body: Close this only if maintainers want https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90378 to own all remaining cron migration semantics, preserving this report as linked evidence.

recommendation.title: Persist Config-Aware Default Owner
recommendation.body: Repair doctor/gateway legacy migration to stamp the configured default agent for missing `agentId`, with regression tests and live upgrade proof for migrated rows and scheduled dispatch.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly tied to the cron SQLite row-codec/store history and the recent owner-attribution cron surface that frames this decision.
